headline: I build AI that survives contact with real systems.
standfirst: Models are easy. The loop around them is the work: evaluate, integrate, instrument, ship reproducibly. My background is deep learning and computer vision in the field — oil palm, maize, disease — and my current practice is LLM applications, retrieval systems, developer tooling and Linux desktops.

positioning.v: Computer vision · LLM apps · RAG · developer tooling
Available for applied AI and systems roles

roles.note: Deep learning for agricultural computer vision in real field conditions. Led a research group of five, co-authored six Scopus-indexed papers including Q1 in Smart Agricultural Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture.
Mentored 25+ students through the Bangkit machine learning track — from notebook to deployed model, with review on evaluation design.
Taught ML, deep learning, data structures and OOP to 200+ students across 14 semesters.

strengths.title: Models meet systems
strengths.body: Wiring models to APIs, databases and interfaces. Backend services, data pipelines, developer tooling, Linux and desktop automation, cross-platform apps. The prototype is the easy half; the operating loop is what I actually do.

strengths.title: Evaluation as a discipline
strengths.body: Training and evaluation workflows from prototype to deployment, with the datasets, experiment tracking and reproducibility that make a result mean something outside the lab that produced it.

strengths.title: Field data, honestly
strengths.body: Oil palm bunches counted in real plantations in East Kalimantan, maize disease under field lighting. Messy, occluded, unlabelled — the conditions where a benchmark number quietly stops predicting anything.

strengths.title: Teach what I learn
strengths.body: Lab teaching and ML mentorship built my habit of writing down the reasoning. If I can't explain a decision to a student, I don't understand it well enough to ship it.

method.body: State the operational question before the model. What decision does this output change?
Smallest end-to-end path: data in, artifact out, no framework left unopened.
Metrics chosen against the failure that actually happens, not the one that flatters the model.
Reproducible builds, pinned data, a run anyone can repeat without me in the room.

publicationsNote: Six papers, four published or in review, two under submission. Q1 venues: Smart Agricultural Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture.

contact.headline: Tell me what you are building.
contact.body: Applied AI work, systems work, or a role where both matter — the fastest route is e-mail. I read everything and reply to anything with a real question in it.

recruiterNote: Recruiter or hiring team: e-mail is fastest. For a role profile, a paper, or a collaboration, the secondary links below go straight to the source.
